author: Bill Ackman
title: Pershing Square Holdings June 2026 Interim Letter to Shareholders
headline: Bill Ackman after a −12.6% half year: with AI hardware driving the market, he bought Visa, Mastercard, Netflix, S&P Global, ICE and Alcon.
summary: Pershing Square Holdings’ NAV fell 12.6% in the first half of 2026 while the S&P 500 rose 10.2%; Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Universal Music were the biggest drags. Ackman and CIO Ryan Israel note that semiconductors and tech hardware, 8% of the index’s companies, delivered nearly 85% of its gains, while nearly 40% of its stocks fell. They used the dislocation to buy six long-followed quality companies: Visa, Mastercard, Netflix, S&P Global, Intercontinental Exchange and Alcon. They expect the portfolio to grow earnings about 20% a year at 19 times earnings, against 12% and 20 times for the S&P 500, and plan more marketing to narrow PSH’s 35% discount to NAV.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: New positions in Visa, Mastercard, Netflix, S&P Global, Intercontinental Exchange and Alcon, companies Pershing has followed for years.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Sold Universal Music Group and Alphabet in the first half and Hertz in July.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Every holding should grow earnings per share by 15% or more a year over three to five years, about half of them by 20% or more.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Microsoft trades at one of its lowest multiples in a decade; Copilot should make Microsoft 365 more resilient to AI than point-solution software.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac fell about 40% this year as privatization stalled; Pershing still expects them to be worth many times today’s prices once it happens.

risks.text: In the short run a falling P/E multiple can swamp earnings growth, producing mark-to-market losses even when businesses do well.
Robotaxis and a strained relationship with Waymo weigh on Uber’s shares.
Investors worry about the heavy AI spending at Amazon, Microsoft and Meta.

quotes.text: We are fortunate in that the current market backdrop has created a highly attractive environment for Pershing Square to deploy capital into new investments.
In the short term, the impact of a reduction in a company’s P/E multiple can easily overwhelm the positive impact of a company’s earnings growth.
We believe PSH is an excellent long-term investment when purchased at NAV.
